proposal.residence_time_basis: total combined volume of Stage-1 and Stage-2 coils at total merged flow rate

streams.notes: NaBr at 10 mol% relative to benzyl alcohol; fully dissolved at RT
2 equiv TBHP ensures full oxidation of benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde and then to benzoic acid intermediate; H2SO4 at 20 mol% activates NaBr in situ to generate Br2/HOBr oxidant
1.5 equiv morpholine relative to benzyl alcohol; introduced at Stage-2 mixer to avoid premature amide formation before oxidation is complete; slight excess drives amidation to completion

proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (PEEK, 0.5 mm bore) at each stage junction
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: S1 and S2 are combined first at Mixer-1 to initiate NaBr/TBHP/H2SO4-mediated oxidation of benzyl alcohol to benzoic acid in Stage-1 coil (7.5 min, 100 °C). S3 (morpholine) is introduced only at Mixer-2 after Stage-1 to prevent competitive amine oxidation by TBHP and to ensure the carboxylic acid intermediate is fully formed before amidation begins in Stage-2 coil (7.5 min, 100 °C). Sequential addition is critical for selectivity.
pre_reactor_steps: Dissolve NaBr (10 mol%) in dioxane with benzyl alcohol; degas with N2 sparging for 5 min
Prepare TBHP/H2SO4 solution in water:dioxane 1:1; handle in fume hood with PPE
Prepare morpholine solution in dioxane; degas
Prime all three pump lines and purge dead volume (~0.5 mL each) before collecting product
Verify BPR set to 6.9 bar to suppress TBHP decomposition vapors and keep dioxane/water mixture liquid at 100 °C (dioxane bp 101 °C; BPR provides safety margin)
post_reactor_steps: Collect effluent into aqueous Na2CO3 (10 wt%) to quench residual TBHP and neutralize H2SO4
Wash organic layer with brine, dry over MgSO4, filter, concentrate in vacuo
Optional: column chromatography (SiO2, EtOAc:hexane 1:1) if purity < 95% by HPLC
Inline IR or UV monitoring at reactor outlet recommended for real-time conversion tracking
proposal.chemistry_notes: The reaction proceeds via a two-step tandem sequence: (1) NaBr/H2SO4/TBHP oxidizes benzyl alcohol to benzaldehyde and then to benzoic acid via in-situ generated hypobromous acid (HOBr) and tert-butoxy radical pathways; (2) the resulting benzoic acid undergoes direct amidation with morpholine, likely facilitated by the acidic conditions and elevated temperature. Flow chemistry advantages include: precise temperature control at 100 °C (above batch 80 °C to compensate for shorter residence time), suppression of TBHP runaway via BPR and small reactor volume, and sequential reagent addition to maximize selectivity. The 15 min total residence time (vs 30 min batch) is feasible due to improved mass/heat transfer in the 1 mm ID tube. Dioxane is retained as solvent for compatibility with the batch protocol; water co-solvent in S2 is necessary to dissolve TBHP (70 wt% aqueous commercial grade).

Stage_1_oxidation.purpose: Oxidation of benzyl alcohol → benzoic acid via NaBr/TBHP/H2SO4

Stage_2_amidation.purpose: Amidation of benzoic acid with morpholine → benzoyl morpholine

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Total 15 min split equally between two stages (7.5 min each). Batch was 30 min at 80 °C; flow at 100 °C with superior heat/mass transfer allows ~2× rate acceleration, consistent with Arrhenius estimate (Ea ~60–80 kJ/mol for radical oxidation gives ~2–3× rate increase per 20 °C). Conservative 15 min chosen to maintain ≥76% yield target.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total merged flow at Stage-2 = 0.4 mL/min (S1 0.1 + S2 0.1 + S3 0.2). Individual pump rates chosen to maintain 0.667 M substrate concentration after mixing and 1.5 equiv morpholine. Low flow rates ensure laminar mixing is adequate in T-mixers at these viscosities.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: 100 °C chosen (vs 80 °C batch) to accelerate kinetics and compensate for halved residence time. BPR at 6.9 bar keeps dioxane (bp 101 °C) and water fully liquid with adequate safety margin. TBHP is stable below 120 °C in dilute solution.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.667 M maintained from batch protocol for direct comparison. Dilution from S2 water co-solvent is accounted for in S2 concentration (1.334 M TBHP pre-mix to achieve ~0.667 M post-merge).
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 6.9 bar (~100 psi) selected to: (a) maintain liquid phase at 100 °C for dioxane/water mixture (vapor pressure ~1.5 bar at 100 °C; 6.9 bar provides 4.5 bar safety margin), (b) suppress TBHP vapor generation (TBHP bp 89 °C at 1 atm; pressurization keeps it liquid), (c) standard BPR setting for 100 °C dioxane systems in literature.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Two-stage PFA coil in series with intermediate T-mixer for sequential reagent addition. PFA chosen for chemical resistance to TBHP, H2SO4, and dioxane at 100 °C.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA: excellent resistance to peroxides, strong acids, and dioxane; rated to >200 °C and >20 bar; transparent for visual inspection.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID: standard for lab-scale flow chemistry; provides Re ~10–50 (laminar) at these flow rates, acceptable for liquid-liquid mixing with T-mixers; minimizes pressure drop.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 6.0 mL total (3.0 mL Stage-1 + 3.0 mL Stage-2). Verification: Stage-1: 3.0 mL / 0.2 mL/min = 15 min ✗ — CORRECTION: Stage-1 flow = 0.2 mL/min, volume = 1.5 mL → 7.5 min; Stage-2 flow = 0.4 mL/min, volume = 3.0 mL → 7.5 min; total volume = 4.5 mL. NOTE: reactor_volume_mL corrected to 4.5 mL in stage_parameters; top-level field states 6.0 mL as nominal including connector dead volume (~1.5 mL). Assumption stated explicitly.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_safety: BPR also acts as a safety device: if TBHP decomposes rapidly, pressure spike is vented through BPR rather than rupturing tubing.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: No photochemistry involved; purely thermal/chemical mechanism.
reasoning_per_field.mixing_order_reasoning: Detailed above; sequential addition prevents amine oxidation and ensures complete oxidation before amidation.
reasoning_per_field.streams_S3_flow: S3 at 0.2 mL/min (double S1/S2) to deliver 1.5 equiv morpholine: [morpholine] × 0.2 = [benzyl alcohol] × 0.1 × 1.5 → [morpholine] = 0.667 × 0.1 × 1.5 / 0.2 = 0.500 M in S3 stock. Assumption: morpholine stock prepared at 0.500 M in dioxane.

safety_flags: TBHP (70 wt% aq): organic peroxide, flammable, oxidizer – store cold, handle in fume hood, avoid contact with reducing agents or metals; use PEEK/PFA wetted parts only
1,4-Dioxane: suspected carcinogen, flammable (flash point 12 °C), forms explosive peroxides on storage – use fresh, inhibitor-free dioxane; ground all equipment
H2SO4: corrosive – use appropriate PPE (face shield, acid-resistant gloves)
Morpholine: flammable, irritant, harmful vapor – handle in fume hood

Elevated temperature (100 °C) + pressurized system (6.9 bar): use rated PFA tubing (burst pressure >50 bar for 1/16 OD PFA), install pressure relief valve upstream of BPR rated at 15 bar, perform pressure test with solvent before reagent introduction
TBHP decomposition risk: do not exceed 120 °C; install thermocouple with automatic pump shutoff if T > 115 °C
Effluent quench: collect into Na2CO3 solution to destroy residual TBHP before disposal; do not collect into closed containers before quench
Dioxane bp 101 °C: BPR must be engaged before heating; never heat open system
Inline pressure gauge required between pump and reactor; if pressure exceeds 10 bar, shut down immediately
All operations in fume hood; no open flames near dioxane lines

confidence.notes: Confidence limited by: (1) exact mechanism of NaBr/TBHP/H2SO4 amidation not fully established in flow literature – may require optimization of NaBr loading and acid equivalents; (2) water co-solvent from aqueous TBHP may affect dioxane miscibility at scale – assume homogeneous at 1:1 v/v; (3) residence time acceleration factor from 80→100 °C is estimated from Arrhenius; experimental optimization of Stage-1/Stage-2 split ratio recommended; (4) morpholine concentration in S3 corrected to 0.500 M (not 0.667 M) – assumption stated in reasoning
